---
title: "How do I smooth noisy measurements with a moving average?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I smooth noisy measurements with a moving average?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Ensure observations have a known regular spacing.

2. Calculate a centered moving average with stats::filter().

3. Draw both raw and smoothed lines with a legend.

## Runnable example

```{r}
days <- 1:12
x <- c(4,8,5,10,7,12,11,15,14,18,16,19)
smooth <- as.numeric(stats::filter(x,rep(1/3,3),sides=2))
plot(days,x,type="b",pch=19,col="#3F78A8",
     xlab="Day",ylab="Measurement",
     main="Original values and 3-day moving average")
lines(days,smooth,col="#A35E20",lwd=3)
legend("topleft",legend=c("Raw","3-day mean"),
       col=c("#3F78A8","#A35E20"),lty=1,lwd=c(1,3),bty="n")
```

## Interpret the result

The second line averages each observation with its immediate neighbors. It is undefined at the first and last day for this centered three-day window.

## Check before applying to real data

Smoothing hides some detail and creates missing values at the edges; it is not evidence that fluctuations were errors.
